Priestlands School
Welcome from the Headteacher
Welcome to Priestlands!
We are very proud of our school and have a thriving and supportive community. Our curriculum is rich, varied and challenging, designed to equip each student with the knowledge and skills necessary for a successful and fulfilling adult life.
Our school motto; Learn More… Do More… Be more… is at the heart of all we do.
We believe all children are capable of making excellent progress and Priestlands has a strong academic record. Our dedicated staff take the time to know each student in a fostering and nurturing environment where learning is engaging, behaviour is positive, and everyone feels safe and valued. With a fantastic array of extra curricular opportunities, trips and competitions, there’s something for every student to explore and enjoy.

Priestlands School
Our values
At Priestlands, we believe that a great education is not just about academic success - we are committed to fostering a supportive and inclusive environment for all students.
We aim to develop students who are Ready, Respectful and Responsible in everything they do. These are the values that guide how we learn, how we behave, and how we treat one another at school.
Ready – with the right equipment, a positive attitude, and excellent punctuality
Respectful – of others’ wellbeing, of teachers and peers, and of our school environment
Responsible – for our learning, behaviour and attendance
These 3Rs are part of our everyday expectations and help us create a safe, positive and supportive community.
We also run a rich Character Education programme, which supports students in developing important life skills and personal strengths. This is built on the nationally recognised Jubilee Centre Framework for Character Education in Schools and focuses on five key areas:
1. Empathy – understanding and caring for others
2. Resilience – learning how to cope with challenges and setbacks
3. Self-Regulation – managing emotions, staying focused, and making thoughtful decisions
4. Integrity – being honest, fair and taking responsibility for your actions
5. Collaboration – working well with others and valuing different views
Through lessons, assemblies, group activities, and school life in general, we help students practise these values every day.
British Values at Priestlands
The British Government has set out five key values to help young people become responsible members of society. At Priestlands, these are part of our daily life:
1. Democracy
We teach students that everyone has a voice. They take part in school decisions by voting for Tutor Reps, the Student Council, and Head Boy and Head Girl. In lessons like History, RE and Ethics, students learn how democracy works and why it matters.
2. The Rule of Law
We help students understand why rules and laws exist—at school, in the community, and across the country. They learn that laws keep us safe and that breaking them has consequences. Respecting rules is an important part of life at Priestlands.
3. Individual Liberty
Students are encouraged to make their own choices and to understand their rights and freedoms. We teach them how to use these safely and responsibly—for example, through E-Safety lessons. We are proud to be a school with a strong anti-bullying culture.
4. Mutual Respect
Respect is at the heart of our school. Students are expected to treat each other with kindness and understand that everyone deserves to be listened to. We show students that respectful behaviour helps everyone learn and thrive.
5. Tolerance of Different Faiths and Beliefs
We celebrate diversity and help students understand and respect different cultures, religions and lifestyles. Through PSHE, Life Skills, assemblies and special awareness days, we create opportunities for students to explore the wider world and their place in it.
Our Goal
We want every student to leave Priestlands with a strong sense of who they are, what they stand for, and how to play a positive role in our community and the world around them.
Priestlands School

Priestlands School
About us
Priestlands is a vibrant and inclusive secondary school committed to providing a high-quality education for all our students. Located in the heart of the New Forest, we take pride in fostering a supportive and ambitious learning environment where every student is encouraged to reach their full potential.
Our dedicated team of staff work tirelessly to inspire, challenge, and support students in both their academic and personal development. With a broad and balanced curriculum, outstanding pastoral care, and a wide range of extracurricular opportunities, we aim to equip our students with the knowledge, skills, and confidence they need for future success.
A broad and enriching curriculum
At Priestlands, we offer an exciting and diverse curriculum that allows students to explore their interests and reach their full potential. From academic subjects to the creative and expressive arts, our students have the opportunity to excel. Our extensive extracurricular programme and school trips further enhance learning, ensuring students have the chance to develop new skills, form friendships, and make lifelong memories.
The Priestlands Path to Progress
Our teaching and learning approach is rooted in the "Growth Mindset" philosophy, which encourages students to embrace challenges, take risks in their learning, and strive for continuous improvement. We believe that the more students learn and experience, the more they grow—and our happiest, most successful students are those who fully engage with all that Priestlands has to offer.
A supportive & ambitious community
At Priestlands, we set high expectations for all our students, not just in their academic work but in their personal growth and contributions to school life. We are proud of our strong sense of community, where students, parents, and staff work together to create a positive and nurturing atmosphere. Whether through academic achievement, sporting success, or creative expression, we encourage all students to develop their talents and aspirations.
Priestlands School

Priestlands School
Languages
Head of Department: Mrs K Stone
At Priestlands, our Languages curriculum is designed to open doors to the wider world by equipping students with the communication skills and cultural understanding they need to thrive in an international society. Weaim to develop confident speakers, attentive listeners, and thoughtful global citizens who are ready to engage with diverse cultures and communities.
Through interactive learning and real-world contexts, students explore how language works, how meaning is conveyed, and how communication shapes our world. They learn to speak, listen, read, and write in anotherlanguage, while also gaining insight into the customs, traditions, and values of other cultures.
Languages are more than just vocabulary and grammar—it’s about thinking critically, understanding perspectives, and building bridges across cultures. Our students gain the linguistic skills and culturalawareness that are valuable in every walk of life.
In our language lessons we strive to give our students a strong foundation in communication, empathy, and cross-cultural awareness.
Choosing Your Path at Key Stage 4
At Key Stage 4, students can deepen their language learning through one or more of the following languages:French, German or Spanish or a mix of the three.
Students study the following three themes:
The exam is divided into the four language skills: Listening, Reading, Speaking and Writing all of equal weighting. Students will build on their knowledge of vocabulary across these themes as well as securing theirgrammar understanding and cultural awareness in French, German and/or Spanish.

Priestlands School
Careers
At Priestlands School, our Careers Curriculum empowers every student to make confident and informed choices about their future. We provide access to high-quality guidance, ensuring that all learners understand the full range of academic and vocational pathways available to them. Through meaningful encounters with professionals, employers and real workplace experiences, students develop the skills, knowledge, and resilience needed to thrive in a changing world of work.
We aim to inspire ambition, challenge stereotypes, and nurture individual strengths and interests, while supporting students to adapt as their goals evolve. By fostering entrepreneurial thinking, preparing them for applications and interviews, and guiding smooth transitions, we equip our students not only to succeed in their next steps, but to leadfulfilling and impactful lives.
For further careers information please see the National Careers Service

DramaHead of Department: Mrs J Strath
We believe that students should have access to a broad and ambitious Drama curriculum, which embeds skills and knowledge of the theatre and performance process, which allows them to develop a love of the performance arts. Our drama curriculum will give students the opportunity to:
devise creative and imaginative performance
appreciate live performance
Facilities
Our purpose built Performing Arts Centre (PAC) with its sophisticated sound and lighting system can seat up to 120 people in tiered seating during our productions and events. During the normal working day we have two working drama studios for our weekly lessons as well as a recording studio, two music teaching rooms, and four music practice rooms.
Priestlands School

Priestlands School
Music
Music at Priestlands: Inspiring Creativity, Confidence, and Collaboration
At Priestlands, we believe music should be a powerful and inclusive force in every student’s education. Our Music Department is dedicated to nurturing creativity, building confidence, and fostering collaboration among students aged 11–16.
Our curriculum is designed to engage and challenge all learners through a rich blend of performance, composition, listening, and analysis. Students explore a wide variety of musical styles and traditions—from classical and folk to jazz, blues, African drumming, Bhangra, Gamelan, and House music. We also embrace music technology, enabling students to compose, record, and produce their own music using industry-standard tools.
We are proud to offer a thriving instrumental lesson programme, with tuition available on every instrument from bassoon to electric guitar. Students are encouraged to take part in a wide range of extracurricular activities, including choir, band, and music clubs. Several concerts and recitals are held throughout the year, giving students regular opportunities to perform and celebrate their progress.
Trips to see world-class performers visiting the area further enrich our students’ musical experiences, broadening their horizons and deepening their appreciation of live music.
Priestlands Music Department has also been selected to be part of the Lead Music School for Hampshire. This prestigious role allows us to help shape the future of music education both locally and nationally, supporting innovation and excellence in schools and communities.
Above all, we want students to enjoy music—to see it not only as a subject but as a lifelong source of expression, connection, and joy.

Priestlands School
Homework
What is Homework?
Homework is work that is set to be done outside the timetabled curriculum. It contains an element of independent study in that it is not usually directly supervised by a teacher. It is important in raising student achievement.
Not all homework is done at home; in fact, for some students who find it hard to work at home, or for some tasks which may require resources (books, software, equipment) more readily available at school, it is necessary or desirable to carry out the task at school.
How is Homework set?
All homework is posted online via Microsoft Teams, part of Microsoft 365. Most students will be familiar with this product. Please see our Microsoft 365 page.
How much homework will be set and how often?
Homework tasks will not always be set in all subjects and those subjects with 2 homeworks per week may combine them into one longer homework, but students will then be given a full week for completion.
Homework tasks should take about 30-40 minutes each.
In Years 10 and 11, homework tasks could each take up to an hour
Satchel One / Show My Homework (SMHW) has been retired.
From September 2024 we will be using Microsoft Teams, part of Microsoft 365.
Most students will be familiar with this product. Please see our Microsoft 365 page.
The website to use is www.office.com , and select Teams from the 'App Launcher' (top left corner) or Apps icon.
When the browser is not supported (you are likely using a phone/tablet) - you will be prompted to download the relevant App for your device.
Parents are not able to access Microsoft 365. Only the student is aware of their school password.
Students with password problems need to see their computer teachers, or IT Support in middle floor Nichols.
If you have successfully used a school computer, you have all the information you need to sign in to M365.
Still having problems? Contact Priestlands ICT Support for assistance

Parents Evening
Each year, there are two opportunities for you to meet your child’s teachers.
In the autumn term, we hold an in-person Meet the Tutor evening at school for all year groups. This event gives you the chance to meet your child’s tutor face to face.
In addition, each year group has a Parents’ Evening, where you can meet with your child’s subject teachers. These meetings take place online.

Priestlands School
Payment System
Tucasi SCOPAY is used for online payments.
Website - http://www.scopay.com/priestlands
Additionally, parents who already have a SCOPAY account are able to login to the SCOPAY app with their existing username and password.
When students join Priestlands, our Finance Team will post a letter home to parents, this includes a unique link code to enable you to register.
If for any reason you have not yet registered for online payments, please contact the finance department on finance@priestlands.hants.sch.uk and they will send you a code to enable you to register.
The account will enable you to make payments online for dinner money, trips and resources. You can also check the history to see purchases made in the canteen. There is no minimum transaction amount for trips and activities, although there is a minimum transaction amount of £10 per child for dinner money. There are no transaction charges.

Priestlands School
Anti-Bullying - Information for Parents
Dealing With Bullying at Priestlands:
Priestlands prides itself on its proactive approach to bullying. PSHCE, Assembly themes and the Life Skills curriculum focus on developing values which support and encourage an inclusive ethos. One of the main focus areas being the development and maintenance of positive relationships as a way to eliminate bullying.
We believe that no school can say that bullying doesn’t happen, however, we believe we deal with bullying effectively and sensitively when it occurs.
We ask that students and parents tell us when there is a concern about bullying as we can only deal with bullying when it is brought to our attention.
Further information regarding ‘bullying’ at Priestlands can be found in the Anti-Bullying Policy in the Policies section of the website.
Concerned about bullying? Speak to someone in school or you can get advice from: Kidscape.org.uk or Bullying.co.uk
